if the heart is enlarged and there are signs of vascular congestion, favor cardiogenic edema."]}, {"category": "comparison", "trigger": "When evaluating pre- and post-operative chest X-rays to assess the resolution of a mediastinal mass and its effect on surrounding anatomy.", "steps": ["Identify the primary abnormality on the pre-operative image, specifically looking for a large opacity in the mediastinum or hemithorax.", "Assess the position of midline structures (trachea, cardiac silhouette) relative to the mass to determine the direction and extent of displacement (mass effect).", "Examine the post-operative image for the absence of the mass and check if the previously displaced structures have returned to their normal anatomical alignment (midline).", "Synthesize findings to confirm that the intervention resulted in both mass removal and structural realignment, distinguishing this from scenarios where only one aspect changed or where other pathologies (like effusion) were the primary feature."]}, {"category": "diagnosis", "trigger": "When evaluating a chest X-ray showing multiple bilateral pulmonary nodules, particularly with peripheral distribution or early cavitation.", "steps": ["Check for the presence of multiple, bilateral, peripheral nodular opacities.", "Assess the nodules for signs of early cavitation (central lucency within the opacity).", "Distinguish from Tuberculosis by confirming the absence of predominant apical/upper lobe consolidation or fibrosis.", "Distinguish from Granulomatosis with polyangiitis by noting the lack of thick-walled, irregular cavities.", "Identify the pattern of peripheral, cavitating nodules as characteristic of septic pulmonary emboli."]}]
